blocks.text: You can connect your Atlassian organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the Atlassian environment.
Atlassian integration consists of the following steps:

blocks.item: Generating an Atlassian API token
Connecting Atlassian to the 3rd-Party App Governance platform

blocks.text: Make sure that the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: A user with Atlassian Admin privileges.
The admin user must have the following product access permissions:
Jira: User Access Admin
Confluence: Product Admin, User Access Admin
Jira Administration: Product Admin
An Atlassian API token is required to retrieve all the relevant information from Atlassian.

blocks.text: Due to the various authentication methods used by Atlassian to retrieve your platform’s information, some functions might not be available without your Atlassian API token.
To generate an Atlassian API token:

blocks.item: Log in to the Atlassian Admin Portal.
Create an API token in Atlassian. To learn more, refer to the Atlassian Documentation.
Note the API token you created. You will need it in the following steps.

blocks.text: For security reasons, you cannot view the API token in plain text. You must store the API token securely.

blocks.heading: Connecting Atlassian to the 3rd-Party App Governance Platform

blocks.text: To connect Atlassian to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: From the drop-down menu, select Atlassian.

blocks.text: See image.
The Add Integration window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Integration window, enter the Atlassian subdomain and the API token created in the previous section, then click Add. An Atlassian subdomain is a unique prefix in the URL for an Atlassian Cloud site (e.g., Jira, Confluence) that identifies your organization's tenant. (For example, in https://acme.atlassian.net, the subdomain is acme.)
See image.
You are prompted to sign in if you haven't already done so.
A consent window appears (all privileges are read-only), and you can see a detailed list of permissions and data.
Click Accept.

blocks.text: See image.

This consent step only allows reading of the apps in your workspace. Additional consent steps are required for the revocation and banning of apps. By default, 3rd-Party App Governance users who are not explicitly granted revocation rights are unable to perform revoke operations.

After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the tenant is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.
You might need to reconnect Atlassian to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired). To reconnect Atlassian to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Reconnect icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.

blocks.item: Click Confirm to continue.

blocks.text: A consent window appears. After consent is granted, the connection is updated.
If you revoke an API token that is currently in use, you can replace it with a new token. To update the API token:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.
In the Edit Integration window, click the Edit icon next to the API token.
Update the API token and click the checkmark to save the changes.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.

blocks.item: Click Confirm if you want to override the connection.

blocks.text: The connection is updated.
You can delete an Atlassian connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete an Atlassian connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.

blocks.item: Click Confirm to continue.

blocks.text: The connection is successfully deleted.
